findings.message: The pyramid is exported as native shapes, not live SmartArt: its entries do not fit PowerPoint's Basic Pyramid at the list's size, so OPF's own pyramid is drawn; OPF's own layout does not hold it either: entry 4 wraps too close to its node's width for PowerPoint to break the same lines.
A matrix needs four entries; its 3 entries are drawn as a grid of cards.
The matrix is exported as native shapes, not live SmartArt: OPF's matrix has no live SmartArt: its text covers 9% of the frame (at most 7.5% matched PowerPoint's text placement).

The cycle is exported as native shapes, not live SmartArt: its entries do not fit PowerPoint's Basic Cycle at the list's size, so OPF's own cycle is drawn; OPF's own layout does not hold it either: OPF's cycle-loop layout did not pass PowerPoint's comparison.

The row of chevrons is exported as native shapes, not live SmartArt: its entries do not fit PowerPoint's Basic Chevron Process at the list's size, so OPF's own row of chevrons is drawn; OPF's own layout does not hold it either: entry 3 wraps too close to its node's width for PowerPoint to break the same lines.

The flow is exported as native shapes, not live SmartArt: its entries do not fit PowerPoint's Basic Process at the list's size, so OPF's own flow is drawn; OPF's own layout does not hold it either: entry 6 wraps too close to its node's width for PowerPoint to break the same lines.

The vertical flow is exported as native shapes, not live SmartArt: its entries do not fit PowerPoint's Vertical Process at the list's size, so OPF's own vertical flow is drawn; OPF's own layout does not hold it either: entry 6 wraps too close to its node's width for PowerPoint to break the same lines.
A matrix needs four entries; its 3 entries are drawn as a grid of cards.

The row of chevrons is exported as native shapes, not live SmartArt: Chinese and Japanese text sits several pixels off in PowerPoint's SmartArt, so OPF's own row of chevrons is drawn; OPF's own layout does not hold it either: OPF's chevron-rows layout passed PowerPoint's comparison for 6 to 8 entries, not 4.

The vertical flow is exported as native shapes, not live SmartArt: Chinese and Japanese text sits several pixels off in PowerPoint's SmartArt, so OPF's own vertical flow is drawn; OPF's own layout does not hold it either: OPF's vertical-flow-columns layout passed PowerPoint's comparison for 5 to 6 entries, not 3.

The 'box-and-whisker' chart is drawn as core's box-per-series fallback: it has one value per category, so its rows form one group and each series is one box of its values, as the preview draws it.

PowerPoint chooses its own contrast color for native funnel value labels and can ignore the written label color (white where the preview uses black). The funnel remains an editable native chart; XML label colors do not establish physical color parity.
